$comment: requires_bootstrap is the call shape this plugin needs: shipped skill text launches scripts as "${BOOTSTRAP_PYTHON:?requires bootstrap >= 0.120.0}", which only bootstrap 0.120.0's SessionStart hook exports. The bootstrap_lib edges (execution_event, interrupt_contract; model_declaration is named only in docs) are degrade-guarded at runtime in execution/events.py and execution/interrupts.py, which probe for absent, too-old or stale and report instead of requiring a newer bootstrap, so they do not raise this floor. content-pipeline-kit's llm/ package consumes the llm_scripting_kit shared lib for the live (openrouter / model-endpoint / claude-cli / codex-cli / opencode-cli) backends, so the owner plugin plugins-kit:llm-scripting-kit must be installed for that lib to be published to _shared_libs. Declaring it install: auto makes opting into content-pipeline-kit pull its dependency automatically -- dependency semantics, distinct from the action-triggered opt-in pattern (bootstrap skill, references/action-triggered-install.md). bootstrap_lib is linked in TRANSITIVELY: CodexCliBackend imports bootstrap_lib.codex (the argv single source of truth) lazily, at dispatch time rather than import time, so without this entry the codex path imports cleanly and then dies on the first call. The llm/ package imports only classify_backpressure from llm_scripting_kit.completion.halt, lazily, first shipped in 0.61.0, which is the min_version of the llm-scripting-kit entry; the edge is DEGRADE (llm/platform.py::_backpressure_classifier), so an absent or too-old lib warns with distinct messages and the gate falls back to exponential backoff. HaltError.retry_after_s is read with getattr and HALT_BACKPRESSURE is a local mirror, so neither is an import. A shared lib does not carry its own shared-lib edges to a consumer -- each venv declares what it needs.
